title: the WSG World of Weather appendix, part 1 - the weather generation system
audit_comment: The Appendix: The World of Weather, part 1 of 2 - the generation system, printed pp. 107-111 plus the extraordinary-precipitation tail that completes the section from the top of printed p. 112. The opener: the Earthlike assumption, the 24-hour day, the 365-or-360 year, four seasons x three months, the counterclockwise rotation, degrees Fahrenheit, feet, mph, wind from whence it blows, the two-tables-one-roll basic structure. The five climatic regions with their latitude bands and wind characters, the seven terrain types, the swamp and scrub/rough translations, the Monster Manual II three-category mesh. The temperature letter codes (the 26-row high/low scale), the Table A1 grid (30 climate/terrain rows x 12 months x the low/mean/high letters, the blank arctic forest row), the Table A2 day-to-day grid (steps, precipitation yes/no/same, the wind increments and sources, the roll-2/12 special rows), the Table A3 precipitation grid (33 rows x 12 season/die-comparison cells). The usage prose: the second-letter start, the daily curve, the stop-at-extreme move, the upper-limit 7-as-6 and the two-day 7-or-8-as-6 streaks with the cold mirror, the die-1/die-2 discipline, the even-roll precipitation consult with the A/B/C columns, the 3-through-11 wind usage with the hemisphere rule, the gust seconds-to-minutes and the half-max rest of day, the 45-mph ceiling with the arctic/tropical 20 and subarctic 25-30 footnotes. The precipitation letter values, the rain-sleet-snow dispatch, the collecting arithmetic (the cylinder, the ounce, the box, the 10-to-1 snow melt), the intensity guidelines (the trace half-hour, the desert one-in-ten, the pan, the dawn/dusk storms, the downpour sandwich) and the extraordinary doubles rule (the 50 percent d6 step-up, the two-double run, the temperate-forest-summer downpour ban, the downpour cap).

consts.name: wwxDayHours
consts.comment: the basic assumptions: a day is 24 hours in duration.

consts.comment: a year is 365 days in length, or thereabouts.

consts.comment: the pole: the arctic climate prevails from 90 degrees, the north or south pole.

consts.name: wwxArcticLoLat
consts.comment: the approximate location of the Arctic Circle: the arctic climate extends from the pole to 66 degrees latitude.

consts.name: wwxSubarcticHiLat
consts.comment: the subarctic climate is typical of areas from 65 degrees latitude (in the northern hemisphere the southern boundary roughly describes the border between the United States and Canada).

consts.name: wwxSubarcticLoLat
consts.comment: the subarctic runs to 51.

consts.name: wwxTemperateHiLat
consts.comment: the temperate climate extends from 50 degrees latitude (the line roughly describing the border between the United States and Mexico).

consts.name: wwxTemperateLoLat
consts.comment: the temperate runs to 31.

consts.name: wwxSubtropHiLat
consts.comment: the subtropical climate predominates from 30 degrees (a line along the southern edge of Mexico).

consts.name: wwxSubtropLoLat
consts.comment: the subtropical runs to 16.

consts.name: wwxTropicHiLat
consts.comment: the tropical climate is the area from 15 degrees.

consts.name: wwxEquatorLat
consts.comment: the tropics run to the equator.

consts.name: wwxArcticWindLightMph
consts.comment: the arctic winds generally blow from east to west and seldom reach greater than moderate velocity - the low bound of the 15-20 mph band.

consts.name: wwxArcticWindModMph
consts.comment: the arctic wind ceiling except during storms, and the Day-to-Day footnote bound: wind velocity in arctic and tropical climatic regions does not exceed 20 mph except in special conditions.

consts.name: wwxSubarcticWindMaxLoMph
consts.comment: the Day-to-Day footnote: in subarctic climate 25-30 mph is the normal maximum - the low bound.

consts.name: wwxSubarcticWindMaxHiMph
consts.comment: the subarctic normal-maximum high bound.

consts.name: wwxWindCeilingMph
consts.comment: except in special circumstances the wind velocity will not increase beyond 45 mph.

consts.name: wwxTempCodeCount
consts.comment: the letter scale runs A through Z, one row per letter.

consts.name: wwxA1Count
consts.comment: the Table A1 grid: 5 climatic regions x 6 terrain rows, 30 rows; the arctic forest row is blank.

consts.name: wwxElevDesertFt
consts.comment: the temperature figures for desert assume an elevation of sea level.

consts.name: wwxElevPlainForestFt
consts.comment: plains and forest figures assume 500 feet.

consts.name: wwxElevHillsFt
consts.comment: hills assume 2000 feet.

consts.name: wwxElevMountainsFt
consts.comment: mountains assume 4000 feet.

consts.name: wwxDegreesPer1000Ft
consts.comment: if the terrain exists at a different elevation, subtract 3 degrees from the temperature figures for every increase of 1000 feet (or add 3 degrees for every decrease of 1000 feet) for a more accurate determination.

consts.name: wwxA2Count
consts.comment: the Table A2 grid: the 2d6 roll 2 through 12, 11 rows.

consts.name: wwxRestOfDayDivisor
consts.comment: wind velocity is the highest speed reached during gusts lasting a few seconds to a few minutes; for the rest of the day the speed will be no more than half the indicated maximum.

consts.name: wwxA3Count
consts.comment: the Table A3 grid: the arctic block carries 5 rows (no forest, no swamp), every other climate 7 - 33 rows x 12 columns.

consts.name: wwxTraceRainEighthInch
consts.comment: trace: less than 1/8 inch of rain.

consts.name: wwxTraceSnowHalfInch
consts.comment: trace: 1/2 inch of snow.

consts.name: wwxLightRainHalfInch
consts.comment: light: up to 1/2 inch of rain.

consts.name: wwxLightSnowInch
consts.comment: light: up to 1 inch of snow.

consts.name: wwxModerateRainQuarterInch
consts.comment: moderate: up to 3/4 inch of rain.

consts.name: wwxModerateSnowInch
consts.comment: moderate: up to 2 inches of snow.

consts.name: wwxHeavyRainHalfInch
consts.comment: heavy: up to 1 1/2 inches of rain.

consts.name: wwxHeavySnowInch
consts.comment: heavy: up to 4 inches of snow.

consts.name: wwxDownpourRainHalfInch
consts.comment: downpour: more than 1 1/2 inches of rain (no snow figure is given - downpour precipitation occurs in certain terrain in subtropical and tropical climates).

consts.name: wwxRainMinF
consts.comment: if the current temperature is 36 degrees or higher, rain will fall.

consts.name: wwxSleetHiF
consts.comment: the sleet band runs from 30 to 35 degrees inclusive - the high bound.

consts.name: wwxSleetLoF
consts.comment: the sleet band low bound.

consts.name: wwxSleetD6Max
consts.comment: in the 30-35 band sleet results half the time (1-3 on d6, or the DM discretion) and snow the other half.

consts.name: wwxOunceTenthCuIn
consts.comment: an ounce of water occupies about 1.8 cubic inches of volume - pinned in tenths.

consts.name: wwxInchRainCuIn
consts.comment: liquid collected in a circular container has volume pi x r squared x h; one inch of rain collected in a 6-inch-radius container yields about 113 cubic inches of water.

consts.name: wwxInchRainOz
consts.comment: the 113 cubic inches come to about 63 ounces of water, or roughly one-half gallon.

consts.name: wwxBoxCuIn
consts.comment: for a square or rectangular container the volume is the product of the three dimensions: a metal box 6 inches by 4 inches by at least 1 inch deep in a 1-inch rainfall holds 6 x 4 x 1 = 24 cubic inches.

consts.name: wwxBoxOz
consts.comment: the 24 cubic inches amount to roughly 13 fluid ounces, somewhat less than a pint.

consts.name: wwxSnowMeltRatio
consts.comment: melted snow converts to water at a rate of 10 to 1: one inch of fresh snow, collected and melted, yields the same liquid as a rainfall of 1/10 inch.

consts.name: wwxTraceMinutes
consts.comment: trace precipitation accumulates to a measurable amount only if the rain falls continuously for at least half an hour.

consts.name: wwxDesertTraceTenths
consts.comment: in a desert, only one out of every ten trace rainfalls will last more than a few minutes.

consts.name: wwxTracePanOz
consts.comment: the heaviest possible trace accumulation, just short of 1/10 inch of rain, even if collected in something as large as a cooking pan 1 foot in diameter, yields less than eight fluid ounces.

consts.name: wwxTracePanTenthInch
consts.comment: the trace ceiling in the intensity prose: just short of 1/10 inch (the letter-code footnote reads less than 1/8 inch - both figures are printed, pinned side by side).

consts.name: wwxHeavyStormWindowHours
consts.comment: heavy precipitation almost always falls in a relatively short time as the result of storm conditions, and in most cases those conditions occur at dawn or dusk - within two hours either way of sunrise or sunset.

consts.name: wwxDownpourBurstInch
consts.comment: the downpour pattern: a period of intense rain during which as much as an inch of water may fall in a half-hour or less, at any time of the day or night.

consts.name: wwxDownpourBurstMinutes
consts.comment: the intense burst lasts a half-hour or less, sandwiched between two periods of lighter, more prolonged precipitation.

consts.name: wwxExtraDoublesRun
consts.comment: whenever two successive rolls on the Day-to-Day Change Table are doubles, and no special weather occurs on either day, the check applies.

consts.name: wwxExtraD6Lo
consts.comment: the extraordinary chance: 50 percent - 1-3 on d6, or the DM discretion.

consts.name: wwxExtraD6Hi
consts.comment: the high bound of the d6 band.

consts.name: wwxExtraStepUp
consts.comment: on a hit, the precipitation for the second day is one step greater than the result given on the Precipitation Variation Table for a roll of doubles.

bools.name: wwxEarthlikeWorld
bools.comment: the system is designed for a world similar, if not identical, to our Earth, assuming most campaign worlds are Earthlike in their fundamental natures.

bools.name: wwxCounterclockwiseFromNorthPole
bools.comment: the planet rotates in a counterclockwise direction, as viewed from a point above the north pole.

bools.name: wwxWindFromWhence
bools.comment: wind direction is the direction the wind is coming from: a north wind blows from north to south, not the other way around.

bools.name: wwxTwoTablesOneRoll
bools.comment: the basic structure: consult only two tables and make a single dice roll to determine the temperature, wind speed and direction, and precipitation for any day except one on which a special weather phenomenon takes place.

bools.name: wwxOptionalPartsSkippable
bools.comment: parts of the system, such as the sections on wind chill and humidity, can be disregarded if the Dungeon Master prefers even more simplicity.

bools.name: wwxEffectsLiveInFirstSection
bools.comment: the system determines conditions but does not explicitly describe the effects in game terms - information on the effects of weather is presented in the first section of this book, for both players and Dungeon Masters.

bools.name: wwxScrubRoughAsPlainOrForest
bools.comment: the DMG terrain translation: consider scrub and rough areas the same (for weather determination) as plain or forest, depending on which of those two the terrain most closely resembles.

bools.name: wwxSevenTerrainTypes
bools.comment: the system considers seven distinct types of terrain as defined in the first part of this book: desert, forest, hills, mountains, plains, seacoast and swamp.

bools.name: wwxArcticMidnightSun
bools.comment: the arctic midnight sun: because the planet rotates around an axis tilted with respect to the sun, there is a period each year in spring and summer when the arctic region is in continual daylight.

bools.name: wwxArcticNoonMoon
bools.comment: the converse: the long arctic winter night, when for an equal length of time in autumn and winter the region is tilted away and in constant twilight. At all latitudes except right at the equator the daylight length varies; only in the arctic are the extremes realized (see the Hours of Daylight Table in the Optional Rules section, the R494 slice).

bools.name: wwxArcticWindsEastToWest
bools.comment: the winds in the arctic generally blow from east to west.

bools.name: wwxArcticPrecipVeryLight
bools.comment: precipitation in the arctic is usually very light if it exists at all; time of year makes no appreciable difference and terrain distinctions are mostly irrelevant since everything is covered with ice.

bools.name: wwxArcticForestImpossible
bools.comment: temperatures for an arctic forest area are not given on the Temperature Variation Table, since vegetation of the normal sort cannot survive in this climate - hence the blank row.

bools.name: wwxSubarcticWinterWindArcticAngle
bools.comment: the subarctic winds in the winter usually blow from the arctic or on a westerly angle from the arctic (northwest in the northern hemisphere, southwest in the southern hemisphere).

bools.name: wwxSubarcticSummerWindWesterly
bools.comment: the subarctic summer wind is more often a prevailing westerly or tropical west wind (southwest in the northern hemisphere, northwest in the southern hemisphere).

bools.name: wwxTemperateWindSeldomEast
bools.comment: temperate winds can blow from the north, south or west, but almost never from the east, except along eastern seacoasts and in localized areas such as the Lake Michigan breeze (see Local Winds in the Optional Rules section, the R494 slice).

bools.name: wwxSubtropicalTradeWinds
bools.comment: subtropical winds are highly variable in velocity and generally blow from the east or from the east and toward the equator - the trade winds that explorers from Europe took advantage of on their journeys to the New World.

bools.name: wwxTropicalWindsDocileTrade
bools.comment: tropical winds are generally docile (except during storms) and most often blow in the same direction as the subtropical trade winds.

bools.name: wwxSwampBareIsPlain
bools.comment: the swamp translation when the category is not specifically mentioned (such as on the Temperature Variation Table): a swamp devoid of large vegetation is a plain.

bools.name: wwxSwampTreesIsForest
bools.comment: a swamp containing trees or other large vegetation is a forest.

bools.name: wwxSwampOceanIsSeacoast
bools.comment: a swamp adjacent to the ocean is seacoast.

bools.name: wwxMmiiColdSplitsSubarctic
bools.comment: the Monster Manual II mesh (it considers only cold, temperate and tropical): divide the subarctic and subtropical areas in half, so monsters of a cold climate occur in the arctic and the part of the subarctic adjacent thereto.

bools.name: wwxMmiiTemperateTakesTheHalves
bools.comment: monsters of a temperate climate occur in any area between the two extremes: the temperate area plus the adjacent half of the subarctic and the adjacent half of the subtropical.

bools.name: wwxMmiiTropicalSplitsSubtropical
bools.comment: monsters of a tropical climate occur in the tropics and the adjacent half of the subtropical area.

bools.name: wwxWinterMonthsAreTwelveOneTwo
bools.comment: the Table A1 month header groups winter as months 12, 1 and 2; spring 3-5, summer 6-8, autumn 9-11.

bools.name: wwxRoll2WindVeryStrong
bools.comment: the roll-2 wind condition reads Very Strong - no numeric increment, consult the Special Weather Table (the R494 slice). NOTE THE SETTLE: this cell is unreadable in all three of our pdf reads and rests on the external transcription.

bools.name: wwxRoll12WindVerySlight
bools.comment: the roll-12 wind condition reads Very Slight - the same consult-the-Special-Weather-Table footnote, and the same settle caveat as the roll-2 cell.

bools.name: wwxDistinctDice
bools.comment: roll 2d6 for each day beyond the present one, day by day or for a number of days in succession; use two dice different in color or size, designated die 1 and die 2 - the distinction matters whenever there is a chance of precipitation.

bools.name: wwxStopAtExtreme
bools.comment: temperature change: move up or down the letter scale as required; if the present temperature is within the allowable range (the first and third letters of the temperature code) but the move would take the result beyond that range, stop when the extreme result is reached.

bools.name: wwxUpperLimitPlusNoChange
bools.comment: if the current temperature is already at the upper limit, treat any plus result as no change.

bools.name: wwxLimitRoll7As6
bools.comment: at the upper limit, treat a roll of 7 the same as a roll of 6 - the temperature drops by 1 step and precipitation is possible.

bools.name: wwxStreakTwoDays7Or8As6
bools.comment: if the temperature remains at the upper limit for two consecutive days, treat a roll of 7 or 8 as a roll of 6, and continue this pattern until the streak of hot weather ends.

bools.name: wwxColdStreakMirror
bools.comment: for a streak of cold weather, perform the same process with the other end of the table.

bools.name: wwxRoll2Or12ConsultSpecial
bools.comment: if the dice roll on the Day-to-Day Change Table is 2 or 12, follow the normal procedure for temperature change, chance of precipitation and wind conditions, and then refer to the Special Weather Table (page 112, the R494 slice) to see if some extraordinary weather occurs.

bools.name: wwxPrecipConsultOnEvenRolls
bools.comment: if the roll of 2d6 on the Day-to-Day Change Table is an even number, refer to the Precipitation Variation Table to determine whether precipitation occurs and how much falls during the next 24 hours.

bools.name: wwxPrecipDieColumns
bools.comment: on a yes result, take the Precipitation Variation column A if die 1 is greater than die 2, column B if the dice are equal, and column C if die 2 is greater than die 1.

bools.name: wwxWindUsedOn3To11
bools.comment: on a dice roll of 3 through 11 the wind conditions column determines the direction and velocity of the wind.

bools.name: wwxArcticWindHemisphere
bools.comment: a wind from the arctic is a north wind in the northern hemisphere and a south wind in the southern hemisphere; the reverse is true for a wind from the tropics.

bools.name: wwxWindIncrementFromPrevious
bools.comment: the velocity increment (+15 mph, +10 mph, etc.) is added to the wind velocity for the previous day; the prevailing direction is as described in the climatic regions text.

bools.name: wwxWindNeverBelowZero
bools.comment: wind velocity cannot fall below zero.

bools.name: wwxGustsSecondsToMinutes
bools.comment: wind velocity is the highest speed the wind will reach on the day in question, during gusts that can last anywhere from a few seconds to a few minutes.

bools.name: wwxSnowBelow30
bools.comment: at a temperature lower than 30 degrees, the precipitation will be a snowfall.

bools.name: wwxSnowOnTheGround
bools.comment: the melt ratio is not especially relevant to collecting drinking water: in most cases when a snowfall occurs the precipitation stays on the ground, from where it can be gathered, and there will usually already be snow cover to scavenge - it is not difficult to obtain drinking water during the snowy season in any climate that has one.

bools.name: wwxDesertTraceFutile
bools.comment: collecting water from a trace rainfall is fruitless except in cases of dire need; in a desert any liquid precipitation quickly soaks through the sandy or rocky soil or evaporates in hot temperatures almost as quickly.

bools.name: wwxLightReadConservatively
bools.comment: light precipitation should be interpreted very conservatively in terrain/climate areas where it represents the greatest amount of rain or snow that normally falls in a day: most such rainfalls are scarcely greater than trace. The converse does not apply where light is the least precipitation possible - there the accumulation can range through the entire span of possibilities.

bools.name: wwxModerateVaries
bools.comment: moderate precipitation does not always fall under moderate conditions: continuous drizzle for most or all of a day, or a storm of only a few minutes; where moderate is the normal maximum, the accumulation is usually not much greater than light and falls as gentle, prolonged rain instead of a brief storm.

bools.name: wwxHeavyAtDawnDusk
bools.comment: heavy precipitation almost always falls in a relatively short time under storm conditions at dawn or dusk, in contrast with the lighter accumulations, which can occur at any time of day or night.

bools.name: wwxDownpourOnlySubtropicalTropical
bools.comment: downpour precipitation occurs in certain terrain in subtropical and tropical climates only.

bools.name: wwxExtraNoTemperateForestSummerDownpour
bools.comment: a downpour will never occur during summer in a temperate forest, regardless of how many times in a row the dice come up doubles - the printed book itself carries the one-in-three erratum in the tail sentence where the rule reads 50 percent.

bools.name: wwxExtraCapsAtDownpour
bools.comment: in no case can extraordinary precipitation exceed the level of a downpour.

bools.name: wwxExtraTwoDoublesThenHold
bools.comment: if doubles are rolled more than twice in succession, the precipitation does not continue to increase but remains at the one-step-greater level, and the d6 chance does not have to be checked any more.

bools.name: wwxSecondLetterStart
bools.comment: at the beginning of an adventure or an episode (such as when player characters find themselves abruptly transported to a different area), use the second letter of the Table A1 code to ascertain the current temperature conditions; from this starting point the temperature moves up or down on a daily basis per the Day-to-Day Change Table.

bools.name: wwxLowBeforeSunrise
bools.comment: as a general rule, the lowest temperature of the day occurs just before sunrise, and the reading gradually rises until the high is reached.

bools.name: wwxHighEarlyAfternoon
bools.comment: the high temperature for the day is reached in early afternoon, possibly remaining at the high point for a few hours at the DM discretion; the reading then decreases gradually through the evening and night until the next low point just before sunrise - modified or disregarded in special weather conditions or when the DM judges different times should prevail.

chains.name: wwxPrecipFormFor
chains.comment: the precipitation form dispatch on the current temperature in degrees Fahrenheit: band 0 = snow (below 30), band 1 = sleet-or-snow (30 to 35 inclusive, sleet on 1-3 of d6), band 2 = rain (36 and above).
